newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares end broadly lower in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares end broadly lower in thin trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly lower on Monday in thin trading led by a decline in small capitalisation shares, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 1.36 percent, or 3.54 points, to 256.03 on low all-share turnover of 110 million shekels against 91 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.51 percent lower at 262.36.
"Today's decline is meaningless since activity was so low. The trend is not clear lately and the market is divided between bulls and bears," said one trader.
"From a technical point of view the trend is still positive but the market is losing momentum and the market rises at a slower pace," the trader said.
A trader at Bank Leumi said the market started rising across the board just before the end of the session and the upward trend was expected to continue on Tuesday.
"There was no evident reason for today's decline which was led by heavy losses of the small capitalisation stocks traded on the Karam (index)," she added.

Blue Square Chain Stores Properties and Investments rose 1.75 percent to 3,406 agorot. The company said on Monday net profit in the fourth quarter of 1996 rose to 24.6 million shekels from 16.1 million shekels a year ealier.

Elbit Medical Imaging surged 4.0 percent to 1,825 agorot. The company said on Monday net profit in the fourth quarter of 1996 rose to $3.2 million from $0.5 million during the same period in the previous year.
Elbit's parent company Elron Electronic Industries fell 1.5 percent to 4,560 agorot.

The most active shares were Israel Chemicals, which rose 0.5 percent to 404 agorot on volume of 9.9 million shekels and Bank Hapoalim, which fell 1.5 percent to 656 on turnover of 3.4 million shekels.
Teva Pharmaceutical Industries dropped 0.25 percent to 21,454 agorot on volume of 2.9 million shekels. On Monday Lehaman Brothers rated Teva a 1-buy.
